title: Day, Night and the Seasons
summary: Two different tilts and spins explain why we have day and night and why summer and winter happen.

steps.title: Earth spins
sentences: Earth spins around like a top once every 24 hours.
The side facing the Sun has day, and the side facing away has night.
The spin makes the Sun seem to rise in the east and set in the west.

steps.title: Earth travels
sentences: While spinning, Earth also travels around the Sun.
One trip takes about 365 and a quarter days, which we call a year.
That extra quarter day is why we add a leap day every four years.

steps.title: The tilt makes seasons
sentences: Earth's axis, the line it spins around, is tilted by about 23 and a half degrees.
When the northern half leans toward the Sun, it gets more direct light and longer days, so it is summer there.
At the same time the southern half leans away and has winter.

steps.title: A common mistake
sentences: Seasons are not caused by Earth being closer to or farther from the Sun.
In fact Earth is a little closer to the Sun in early January, when it is winter in the north.
It is the tilt that matters.

facts: Near the equator the days and nights stay about 12 hours long all year.
At the poles the Sun can stay up for months, and then stay below the horizon for months.
Earth spins at about 1,600 kilometres per hour at the equator.

quiz.why: Earth's spin turns each place toward and away from the Sun every 24 hours.
The tilt changes how directly sunlight hits each half of Earth during the year.

quiz.q: How long does Earth take to go once around the Sun?
quiz.why: One trip around the Sun is a year.
